subject: Lumera pilot: output title, retrain opt-out, and feedback lockbox
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@lumerahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@lumerahealth.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Request: MSA redlines around output & retrain rights

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Lumera is excited to move the pilot forward. Attached are our proposed redlines to the MSA and Order Form (see Lumera_MSA_redlines_20260928.pdf). The key commercial/legal asks from our side are short and listed below:

- Output ownership: Lumera requests assignment of title to any model outputs (generated content) produced by Redwood for Lumera workloads.
- Retraining: Lumera requires an explicit opt-out so that Redwood will not use Lumera data/outputs to retrain or improve any Redwood-wide models without a separate agreement.
- Feedback license: Lumera is willing to provide telemetry/feedback for operational improvements but only via a named "lockbox" arrangement — any use must be scoped to the Lumera instance and cannot be used for commercial models without written consent.
- Evidence/escrow: Lumera wants a practical evidence route (audit logs or redacted telemetry) showing Redwood's compliance for a 90-day retention window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these principles as a baseline? If not, please identify the exceptions and propose alternate language. We'd like to get this to legal today to avoid slipping the procurement window.

Thanks,
Sophie Chen
Procurement Lead, Lumera Health
Sophie.Chen@lumerahealth.com

Attachment: Lumera_MSA_redlines_20260928.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@lumerahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: MSA redlines around output & retrain rights

Hi Sophie — appreciate the clear list. Looping in our legal and deal desk to make this concrete. High-level responses below and an internal redlines summary attached (redlines_summary_20261001.xlsx):

- Output ownership: We can accept customer ownership of outputs for the Lumera account (i.e., Lumera holds title to content generated from your prompts). We typically carve out a limited right to retain aggregated telemetry for debugging and perf monitoring, not for downstream productization.
- Retraining / retrain opt-out: We support an opt-out for using Lumera data/outputs in Redwood-wide model retraining. If Lumera wants Redwood to provide model improvements (fine-tuning) later, that would be handled under a separate SOW.
- Feedback license / lockbox: Our proposed pattern: Lumera grants Redwood a narrow, non-exclusive feedback license limited to "operational quality improvements" for Lumera's deployment only. Redwood will segregate that feedback in a technical lockbox and will not use it to update any public/shared models without explicit written consent.
- Evidence/escrow: We can provide audit logs and a compliance runbook; we retain request logs and token-level telemetry for 90 days by default and can arrange a provision for redacted log export or independent review under an NDA.

Laura — can legal propose concrete wording for the MSA/Order Form and confirm whether the lockbox language is achievable from a technical and legal standpoint?

Sophie — if this aligns, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope with the order form + exhibit and route to your procurement team by EOD.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: redlines_summary_20261001.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@lumerahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: MSA redlines around output & retrain rights

On Oct 1, 2026, Neha Kapoor wrote:
> Laura — can legal propose concrete wording for the MSA/Order Form and confirm whether the lockbox language is achievable from a technical and legal standpoint?

Hi all — thanks for the context. Below are three pragmatic options (we recommend Option A or B) and proposed clause snippets to put into the MSA/Order Form. Please confirm which you prefer so we can produce a clean redline.

Option A (Recommended):
- Customer owns output title for the Services ("Customer Output").
- Customer may opt-out of Redwood using any Customer Data, including Customer Output, to train or improve Redwood models ("Retrain Opt-Out").
- Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use feedback and telemetry solely to provide and operate the Services for Customer ("Operational Quality License"). Redwood will segregate this feedback in a named technical lockbox that is logically and operationally segregated from Redwood model training pipelines and will not use the data to train general-purpose or commercial models without Customer's prior written consent.

Proposed clause (for insertion):
"Customer Output Ownership and Feedback License. Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to Customer Output. Customer may elect, in writing, to opt-out of Redwood using Customer Data (including Customer Output) to train or improve any Redwood-owned models. If Customer elects not to opt-out, Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use Customer Data solely for operational quality improvements of the Services provided to Customer. Such feedback shall be stored in a named lockbox and shall not be used to train Redwood-wide models unless Customer provides separate written consent.

Evidence and Audit. Redwood will retain request and telemetry logs for a minimum of 90 days and will provide redacted exports or permit an independent auditor review under a mutually agreeable NDA and SOW.

Notes / Exceptions:
- We cannot provide retroactive exclusivity for general model training of features already produced by public model releases.
- If Lumera requires exclusive ownership for derivative model re-deployments (e.g., transfer of a trained model instance), that should be covered by a separate SOW with pricing and support terms.

If Lumera agrees to Option A, drafting team will produce clean redlines and an exhibit describing the lockbox technical controls (encryption, access controls, labeling).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai"

From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@lumerahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@lumerahealth.com
Date: 2026-10-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: MSA redlines around output & retrain rights

Neha / Laura — thanks, that framing is really helpful. Lumera is comfortable with Option A as long as three follow-ups are included:

1) Confirmation that the lockbox will be logically isolated and that only named Redwood engineers supporting the Lumera account can access it.
2) A 90-day retention period for telemetry (as noted).
3) A DocuSign-ready Order Form showing the pilot price and the retrain opt-out box checked, plus the lockbox exhibit.

We are ready to sign today if you can produce the clean redline and the DocuSign envelope. I've attached the countersigned order form for reference.

Sophie Chen
Procurement Lead, Lumera Health
Sophie.Chen@lumerahealth.com
